name: Pythagorean Theorem (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that accepts two input values from the user, one for each side of a right-angle triangle. The program uses the Pythagorean theorem (c^2 = a^2 + b^2) to calculate the length of the triangle's hypotenuse.

comments.content: We need to read and process the values that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the length of side A.
We need to read the length of side A that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the length of side A by calling the nextDouble() method because the length could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.
We prompt the user to enter the length of side B.
We need to read the length of side B that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the length of side B by calling the nextDouble() method because the length could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.
To compute the length of the triangle's hypotenuse, we need to first compute the square of side A. We square side A by calling the Math.pow method.
Note that Math.pow(a, b) is a method that takes the value of the first argument a and raises it to the power of the second argument b. The returned value is a double.
To compute the length of the triangle's hypotenuse, we need to compute the square of side B too. We square side B by calling the Math.pow method.
Note that Math.pow(a, b) is a method that takes the value of the first argument a and raises it to the power of the second argument b. The returned value is a double.
We use the Pythagorean theorem to obtain the length of the triangle's hypotenuse. To get the triangle's hypotenuse, we take the square root from the sum of square of side A and square of side B.
Note that Math.sqrt(a) method calculates the square root of the argument a. The returned value from the sqrt() method is a double.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the length of the triangle's hypotenuse. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given strings and value of the variables.
